theorems.statement: One Link ontology and one abstract Link-forming primitive induce exactly four local self-incidence structural cases; after an oriented Context these are ROOT, START_K, END_K and PAIR.
assumptions: F2F3OneSidedExistence for grounded realizability of one-sided/root-basis witnesses
theorems.scope: Local four-case self-incidence classification plus grounded realizability witnesses. The classifier itself is proposition-level; Context orientation only names the one-sided cases after classification.
theorems.exclusions: No host enum, codec digit, host handle equality, Memory canonical-map identity, or four-opcode implementation may serve as classification authority. External proof must separate the four proposition-level combinations from implementation decidability. FND-01 does not include arbitrary-Link pole extensionality: ordered-pole identity is the separate FND-13 theorem on its explicit finite Grounded normalization domain. Context orientation only names the two one-sided cases after the structural partition exists.

theorems.statement: Full self-closure X = X ⟼ X is unique in the accepted foundation and determines R.
theorems.scope: Unique full self-closure from explicit A1RecursiveSeparation. FullSelf supplies Grounded evidence internally via grounded_of_full_self; callers do not supply F2/F3 normalization or FND-13.
theorems.exclusions: Do not assume FND-13 pole extensionality, F2F3 normalization, canonical Memory pair identity, host handle equality, or root uniqueness itself.

theorems.statement: On the accepted finite R-grounded semantic Link domain, Link identity is determined by ordered poles: x = y iff start(x) = start(y) and finish(x) = finish(y). Constructor injectivity form(A,B) = form(C,D) iff A = C and B = D follows directly from the primitive projection laws.
assumptions: Grounded evidence for both Links under comparison
theorems.scope: Inherited A6 structural-identity theorem on admissible semantic Links with explicit finite R-grounding evidence.
theorems.exclusions: Technical handles, storage addresses, canonical-map keys, or host object identity are not semantic equality. FND-02 unique ROOT is not a premise of FND-13 unless a future derivation uses it substantively. A stronger arbitrary-Link extensionality theorem may be used only under an explicitly supplied global normalization-completeness premise and is not the accepted FND-13 domain statement. Ungrounded distinct-node cycles remain outside this theorem scope.

theorems.statement: R/O/C/L are derived structural representatives of the accepted Link foundation under an orientation convention, not four independent ontology primitives.
theorems.scope: Accepted root/aspect basis with v0.14 Context-relative orientation semantics.
theorems.exclusions: Symbolic names R/O/C/L and implementation handles are not semantic authority.

theorems.statement: U = C ⟼ O is an ordinary PAIR-derived representative and not a fifth self-incidence class.
theorems.scope: Accepted root basis.
theorems.exclusions: U is not a fifth recursive alphabet symbol or ontology primitive.

theorems.statement: Canonical recursive structural description is unique on its explicitly declared finite ROOT-decomposable carrier domain.
theorems.scope: Current finite inductive recursive-description totality/uniqueness is stated on Grounded Links with an explicit finite recursive-carrier decision. #1797 provides a paired-kernel concrete non-Grounded cycle falsifier for all-Link totality.
theorems.exclusions: Do not extend totality/existence to arbitrary non-well-founded distinct-node cycles. Generic description functionality remains meaningful only when derivations exist. Sequential Anum/Q identity is separate.

theorems.statement: Accepted structural transport/reconstruction is invariant under fresh local Memory handles within its declared transport domain.
theorems.scope: Accepted recursive structural transport and exact declared carrier boundaries.
theorems.exclusions: Memory addresses/handles are not semantic identity and this does not grant semantic materialization authority.

theorems.statement: Accepted contextual truth separates three roles: L=O⟼C is the root truth-value aspect, current K⟼A is the Context-specific truth witness, and current K⟼A plus current A⟼B propagates to current K⟼B under the accepted A16 Scope-composition law.
assumptions: CurrentScopeMember as the external projection of the published current Scope
ContextualScopeCompositionLaw as the accepted A16 semantic premise
theorems.scope: Accepted contextual-truth execution layer inherited from v0.13 A16 and preserved by v0.14/V14-L11.
theorems.exclusions: Ambient Memory existence alone is not truth in Context. The semantic role of L is an accepted contextual-truth premise, not derived from bare Foundation. CurrentScopeMember is only an external Prop-valued projection and no host Set/Bool/map becomes truth authority.

theorems.statement: Generalized relational reaction separates selected-Theory admission/match from emitted image: from current K ⟼ {A_i}, every admitted applicable positive emission contributes K ⟼ B, unmatched current members survive, an explicitly matched empty image remains distinct from no match, and reaction occurrence remains distinct from extensional successor membership so active identity is not quiescence.
assumptions: FND-07 current contextual-truth boundary only; selected Theory relations are not CurrentScopeMember rules
SelectedTheoryReactionSemantics as the accepted V14-L11/V14-L4 admission/match/emission/reaction premise
theorems.scope: Accepted generalized modus ponens/reaction scope covering no-match preservation, explicit 1→0, 1→1, 1→N, N→1, N→M, active identity versus quiescence, and mixed stable/active Scope behavior.
theorems.exclusions: Do not collapse NO_ADMITTED_RELATION into explicit ZERO; ambient Link existence is not admission authority; selected-Theory admission must not be reclassified as CurrentScopeMember/ContextualRule merely to reuse FND-07 composition; ContextualScopeCompositionLaw is not an FND-08 reaction premise; Produced output is not the whole successor because unmatched current members survive; extensional Next=Active does not imply quiescence; no unrestricted host rewrite/global substitution, host RuleKind, multivalued-function primitive or result-cardinality opcode is implied.

theorems.statement: ZERO/ONE/MANY and generalized N→M are derived properties of admitted relational images only after separating Matched(A) from emitted Image(A,B): NO MATCH preserves currentness, explicit ZERO is a matched empty image, active identity remains a real reaction even when successor membership is unchanged, and duplicate paths converge extensionally by semantic Link identity.
theorems.scope: Accepted generalized relational execution, including the NO MATCH versus explicit ZERO boundary, ONE/MANY image cardinality, active identity versus quiescence, N→1 convergence, N→M union and mixed stable/active reactions.
theorems.exclusions: Do not introduce a hidden multivalued-function or result-cardinality semantic primitive; do not equate absence of emitted B with absence of an admitted match; an explicit ZERO is zero contribution from that matched antecedent and does not imply global absence of the same semantic Link if another derivation emits it; provenance multiplicity is not semantic successor multiplicity.

theorems.statement: Recursive inversion J is defined directly on Link structure by J(A ⟼ B) = J(B) ⟼ J(A), with exact treatment of self-incidence cases.
theorems.scope: Unique total recursive inversion graph on the declared finite Grounded source domain.
theorems.exclusions: Host field order, graph labels, or codec digits are not the semantic definition of J. No all-Link totality claim: #1797 establishes NECESSARY_RESTRICTION for current finite inductive totality/existence on a concrete non-Grounded distinct-node cycle. Generic functionality remains conditional on derivation existence.

theorems.statement: Recursive inversion is involutive on its stated domain: J(J(X)) = X.
theorems.scope: Involution on the exact Grounded domain of INV-01, using only Grounded normalization/pole reconstruction.
theorems.exclusions: No arbitrary-Link/global-normalization premise and no claim for non-Grounded distinct-node cycles.

theorems.statement: ROOT is fixed by recursive inversion.
theorems.scope: Declared recursive inversion domain.

theorems.statement: Recursive inversion exchanges the two proper one-sided self-incidence orientations without identifying them.
theorems.scope: Declared recursive inversion domain; semantic START_K/END_K names remain Context-relative.
theorems.exclusions: This does not select a Foundation-global absolute START side.

theorems.statement: PAIR remains in the PAIR class under recursive inversion while its poles are recursively exchanged.
theorems.scope: Declared finite Grounded recursive inversion domain.
theorems.exclusions: PAIR preservation uses the already proved involution and one-sided exchange results; no independent pair-preservation axiom or global arbitrary-Link extensionality is assumed.

theorems.statement: On the accepted root basis, J fixes R, exchanges O/C under the chosen orientation, and fixes L/U structurally.
theorems.scope: Accepted root-basis representative calculation; orientation labels are not absolute ontology.
theorems.exclusions: This basis calculation alone is not a proof of full Theory automorphism.

theorems.statement: Objective chirality survives inversion: J reverses orientation while preserving the structural distinction between the two one-sided self-incidence classes.
theorems.scope: Accepted v0.14 chirality/orientation structure.
theorems.exclusions: Chirality is not a globally privileged orientation selected by an observer.

theorems.statement: Objective chirality Ω={W,J(W)} exists before observation; an oriented Context K selects χ(K), inducing local START_K/END_K roles, and relative frame transport g_AB∈{Id,J} composes as Z2.
theorems.scope: Accepted v0.14 Context-relative A4′ orientation law.
theorems.exclusions: No Foundation-global selected W, ExactSequence, host boolean, raw InR/OutR presence, four primitive opcodes, or stronger arbitrary-Link normalization are orientation authority.

theorems.statement: Semantic Link identity is structurally immutable: equality of formed Links preserves both ordered poles, and changing either pole denotes a distinct semantic Link. Rewrite/execution may replace selected membership or explicitly construct structurally substituted Links, but does not mutate an existing Link's poles in place.
theorems.scope: Accepted v0.14 structural Link identity and rewrite/membership boundary, independent of Grounded recursion and physical storage identity.
theorems.exclusions: No claim about physical object immutability or retention/deletion policy; constructing a new Link and replacing selected membership are allowed; existing dependents are not silently rewritten, while explicit child substitution forms new dependent Links. No FND-13, Grounded, Memory-handle or host object-identity premise is required.

theorems.statement: Representation identities are separated: Anum is a rooted sequence representation family, ExactSequence preserves exact positional identity distinct from fold denotation, the recursive Link codec is not Anum, Q is a versioned sequence codec/interpreter, and every local sequence origin is R.
assumptions: AcceptedV014RepresentationDefinitions external projection of accepted representation contracts
theorems.scope: Accepted v0.14 representation/codec boundary plus post-acceptance #1583 capability clarification.
theorems.exclusions: No claim that recursive structure and Q are globally isomorphic or that a shorter source globally dominates a stronger representation contract. No representation-strength ranking and no host representation classifier is promoted into MTS ontology.

theorems.statement: Under the accepted V14-L14 representation-layer boundary and the proved FND-01/FND-11 dependencies, structural roles and representation denotations remain over the sole semantic Link carrier; recursive structure, representations/codecs, byte-text and symbolic metanotation introduce no second ontology entity.
theorems.scope: Accepted v0.14 representation-layer ontology boundary cross-checked against FND-01 Link-only structural roles and FND-11 representation-identity separation.
theorems.exclusions: The theorem does not derive ontology policy from host Type inequality, an enum, Bool flag, or identity ranking. Representation/source objects may have distinct local identities and need not themselves be Links; only their accepted semantic structural/denotational authority remains grounded in the sole Link ontology.
